title: Error root-cause tree and service pressure dashboard
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a unified, production-grade dashboard and canonical root-cause taxonomy for runtime errors across the inference stack. The goal is a browseable root-cause tree (transport, overload, timeout, model-inference, response-validation, client-errors, infra) backed by tracing hooks and metric/log pipelines, plus a companion Service Pressure heatmap that surfaces overload and queuing hotspots by route/model/region.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical error taxonomy documented and approved by SRE/Runtime/SDK teams
Tracing instrumentation added at router, scheduler, and inference-core boundaries to emit standardized error tags (error_class, error_subclass, model_version, kernel_hint)
Pipeline enrichment implemented: traces correlate to metrics and logs via request_id and sampled index
Grafana dashboard delivered: Root-cause tree view + Service Pressure heatmap with filters by route/model/region and time range
Dashboards include drilldown links to representative traces, relevant GitHub PRs, and runbook steps
SLO/alert thresholds defined for top-3 error classes and validated on staging traffic
updates: 2025-11-02 Kickoff: aligned cross-functional owners (SRE: Alex Rivera, Runtime: Liam Chen, SDK: Priya Singh). Agreed taxonomy draft during sync.
2025-11-04 Prototype: sketched root-cause tree UI and Service Pressure heatmap in Figma (link in artifacts). Focus on surfacing overload vs model-degraded behavior separately.

2025-11-06 Instrumentation spike: added trace hooks in request-router and inference-invoke path. Emit span attributes: error_class, http_status, grpc_code, model_error_code, queue_time_ms, kernel_type.

2025-11-08 Pipeline decision: use adaptive sampling for traces (1% baseline, up to 20% on error spikes) to bound cost. Metrics (histograms/counters) sent at 10s resolution; logs forwarded for error_class="model" with full payload hash redaction.

2025-11-11 Dashboard build: initial Grafana panels for error distribution and heatmap of qps vs queue_time published to staging (grafana://dash/OBS-press-01). Linked drilldowns to trace viewer with request_id correlation.

2025-11-13 Review feedback: PM & SRE requested clearer separation between transient timeouts (upstream/backoff) and sustained overload. Decided to add a rolling window ratio metric: timeouts_per_minute vs concurrency_utilization.
2025-11-15 Runbook: drafted triage steps for top three classes (timeout, overload, model_error). Includes automated rollback suggestion to older model_version for model_error spikes.

2025-11-18 Work in progress: preparing PR to central metrics-enricher service and finalizing alert thresholds for P90/P99 latency and error rate per route. Planning A/B rollout to 10% of traffic next week.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Sampling vs cost: chosen adaptive sampling to preserve signal for error spikes while keeping storage costs manageable
Cardinality: limited dimension explosion by only tagging model_version and kernel_type at ERROR spans; non-error spans have coarser labels to reduce metric cardinality
Enrichment location: decided to enrich traces in the router (pre-inference) to attach route and tenant metadata rather than post-facto joins in BI to reduce join latency
Dashboard complexity: prefer a focused set of panels with deep drilldowns rather than an all-in-one giant canvas to keep SRE playbook alignment simple
next_steps: Finish metrics-enricher PR and roll to staging (ENG-25419-PR1)
Add sample-and-enrich agent to inference nodes to tag model_error_code and kernel_hint in spans
Finalize Grafana variables and add keyboard shortcuts for quick drilldowns
Runback experiment: enable on 10% traffic and validate alert sensitivity against known synthetic fault injections
Schedule 1-hour runbook tabletop with CS/Support to validate playbook clarity
notes: Important: ensure payload redaction (PII) is applied in the log forwarder when model_error logs are collected - runtime and security already aligned on redaction rules
Consider future iteration to surface model degradation cause (quantization vs kernel fallback) by ingesting kernel-level counters from inference runtime
